hardened_runtime_v1643: v16.4.3 (SEC-201..207 + OPS-001..003 closed; evidence in docs/research/RUNTIME_SECURITY_CLOSURE_V1643.md, threat model in docs/research/THREAT_MODEL_V1643.md): one SQLite authority store (WAL, synchronous=FULL, BEGIN IMMEDIATE) owns durable single-use grant reservations (unique id/nonce/digest/activation), the hash-chained signed event log, idempotent request outcomes, audit, and the active pointer — atomic across threads, processes, restarts, and crashes, fail-closed on store unavailability. PrincipalContext derives roles from authenticated peer uids (never request fields); research.sock/operator.sock enforce per-operation whitelists in the dispatcher and audit allowed+refused decisions. Recovery separates LAST_COMMITTED from live serving: cold start is UNAVAILABLE; recover() re-verifies the log, qualification, revocation freshness, and artifacts, obtains fresh admission, probes health, then commits before routing; rollback re-checks the revocation epoch and only targets verified-live predecessors. RuntimeBackendManifestV1 binds backend id, implementation digest, dependency lock, inference config, qualification digest, and policy epoch. The service bounds request size (pre-parse), connections, per-principal quotas, and execution time over a fixed worker pool with deadlines. ServingRouter routes infer() traffic only to the committed+healthy instance under one lock — supervised activation now reaches real inference
